checked_sources: Independent finite Liouville divisor convolution and exact products
correctness.rationale: An even solution has odd beta(n), so every odd-prime exponent is even: n=2^a t^2 with t odd. For at most eight primes dividing t, the first eight odd primes minimize the product of p/(p+1) and give beta(t^2)/t^2>2/5; t=1 also satisfies the bound. The factor beta(2^a)/2^a is at least 1/2, so the positive odd quotient (n-1)/beta(n) is below 5. If the quotient is 3 then n=1 mod 3, forcing even a and 3 not dividing t. Omitting 3 from the smallest eligible primes gives beta(t^2)/t^2>1/2, and even a gives beta(2^a)/2^a>2/3, contradicting quotient 3. For t>1, beta(n)<(2^a-1)t^2<n-1, ruling out quotient 1; for t=1, the explicit power-of-two formula leaves only 2 and 4. An independent divisor convolution beta(n)=sum over d|n of d times Liouville(n/d) gave only 2 and 4 through 500000 among even inputs. Independent exact products gave 1062347/2654208, 30808063/59719680, and 20928465245153916450 for twice the square of the first nine odd primes. The finite computation corroborates but does not establish the unrestricted argument; the submitted script was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: Necessary condition only, with no conclusion for odd n or existence when ten or more primes divide n.

originality.rationale: The square odd part is known: it follows immediately from Tóth's published parity characterization and is also explicit in the October 13 Resultary proof. That proof uses a closely related odd-quotient and prime-product argument, and its even conclusion is only omega(n)>=5 for n>4. The supported distinct contribution is the tightening to omega(n)>=10 and the resulting explicit size bound. In particular, tracking the valuation of 2 after quotient 3 is forced to be a multiple of 3 is not needed in the earlier three-odd-prime argument but supplies the stronger factor bound here. No inspected source gives the ten-prime implication for even beta solutions.
residual_risks: Unindexed stronger beta bounds remain possible. The early arXiv extraction omits the exception 4; the journal formulation explicitly includes it. Full 1932 Lehmer text was not accessed, and it concerns a different equation on these candidates.

value.rationale: Improving the earlier five-prime even obstruction to ten is a substantial unrestricted exclusion, obtained without any exponent cap. The parity-dependent treatment of the quotient exposes an arithmetic constraint absent from a finite search and supplies a concrete lower bound on n. This advances the posed beta analogue without claiming to settle it or treating the known parity characterization as the contribution.
